newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian money rates help front end of OLO curve.
newsitem.headline: Belgian money rates help front end of OLO curve.

text.p: The Belgian central bank has begun pumping liquidity back into the money market after last week's blow out in Treasury bill yields, dealers said on Monday.

Since last Wednesday the central bank has been offering liquidity twice a day through intraday repo operations, whereas normally such operations are only carried out once, one trader said. The central bank was not immediately available to comment.

The extra liquidity helped relieve the pressure on money market rates on Monday, leading also to the front end of the linear bond curve to steepen sharply. One money market trader said he believed there was more room to go lower.
One week repos fell back to 3.44/48 percent on Monday from 3.48/51 percent on Friday with three month Treasury bill yields moving to 3.46/50 percent from 3.50/54 percent.
One money market trader noted the central bank's move followed the rise in Treasury bill yields at last Tuesday's auction to 3.57 percent from 3.42 percent.

One OLO trader said news the government had successfully reviewed its 1997 budget contributed to the move. But the budget news had no impact on the Belgian franc, which was trading at a little changed 20.6325/35 to the mark in late Monday trade, still weaker than its ERM midpoint to the mark of 20.6255.
Longer-dated linear bonds were pulled higher by Bunds early but had pared gains by midday ahead of the Treasury's monthly OLO auction and Tuesday's U.S. Fed policy meeting.
A relatively light 17 billion of francs of OLOs were sold at the auction, with 12 billion in the benchmark March 2007 bond.
The 10-year benchmark yield ended at 6.04 percent, down from 6.07 percent on Friday.
Dealers said a 25 basis point rate hike at Tuesday's FOMC meeting was fully priced into markets. Only a 50 basis point hike could have negative implications, they said.
